Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. review_evidence: src/Tools/Haskell/Haskell.thy (3931 lines): 34 generate_file commands emitting Haskell modules Isabelle/Bytes.hs through Isabelle/Cache.hs (XML, YXML, Server, Bash, Options, Isabelle_Thread), then export_generated_files; no lemma or definition.
src/Tools/Haskell/Test.thy: imports Haskell with condition ISABELLE_GHC_STACK; only compile_generated_files with an ML function that runs 'isabelle ghc_stack build'.
src/Tools/Profiling.thy: one ML block defining structure Profiling (locale/theorem counts, ML heap sizeof statistics, args.yxml/result.yxml I/O) and ML_command Profiling.main ().

justification: This file is excluded only because an accepted repository-review record targets its exact current content through an exact path, exact path set, or literal subtree prefix. The review record is pinned to the reviewed work-unit snapshot and records the repository-local rationale, content-level losslessness invariant, evidence, selector, and source provenance. FD-018 authorizes no filename, path role, generated directory, or cross-repository class by itself; any changed work-unit snapshot makes the review stale and blocks indexing until it is re-audited.
title: Repository-local audited exclusion

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
title: Parser-verified Lean import-only module retained

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, and lakefile.toml are non-formal package/build metadata rather than proof-assistant source. They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.
title: Non-formal Lean build/toolchain metadata

All occurrences therefore remain physically indexable for source/path queries. The public API collapses exact duplicate hits into one result and returns every occurrence as an alias. Physical content deduplication is deferred until alias paths can themselves participate in retrieval without loss.

justification: README and source-documentation files outside the proof assistant's formal-source extensions can contain useful project terminology, provenance, references, and navigation, but they do not themselves constitute proof-assistant declarations or proofs. They are removed only from the primary mathematical-content index and retained in the auxiliary documentation/navigation index. A formal-source file such as README.lean, README.thy, README.agda, or Readme.lsp is never covered by this decision merely because of its basename.
title: Non-formal README or source documentation

justification: Tree-sitter verification establishes that these Lean files own no declaration or proof, but that fact alone does not make their module names, paths, comments, provenance, or import topology dispensable search signals. FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.

They remain in the source checkout for reproducibility but are not fed to either mathematical or documentation search. A formal Lean build script such as lakefile.lean is ordinary Lean source and is explicitly outside this decision: corpus audit found many such files containing definitions, structures, inductives, examples, and even axioms, so the filename alone cannot prove absence of useful formal prior art.

ProofStepPlan consumes that AST for step-level navigation. All content is meta-level tooling.
evidence.rationale: These three files are the core of the tactic parsing infrastructure for editor/LSP tooling. They define, parse, pretty-print, and structurally navigate tactic syntax trees ('a tac_expr) — ML-level representations of tactic source code. They contain zero HOL object-logic declarations, theorems, definitions, or proof terms.

FD-005 assumed those signals remained searchable through a deployed auxiliary navigation index. The production search service does not currently publish or query that index, so excluding these files from primary search violated FILTER-007's preservation requirement. Keep them in primary search, while also retaining the auxiliary copy, until an end-to-end searchable auxiliary channel is deployed and measured.
